extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO examiners and formalities staff; Member States' industrial property offices and industrial property agents
extracted.subtask_description: Official guidelines for examination of ARIPO patent applications and registered utility models covering formal requirements, search, substantive examination, special chemistry/biotechnology provisions, and general procedural matters. Intended to instruct ARIPO staff (and inform national offices and agents) on practice, time limits, filings, and substantive patentability assessment under the Harare Protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how applications may be filed (Rule 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO application may be filed with either the ARIPO Office or the Industrial Property Office of any contracting state, if the national law of the contracting state so permits. A divisional application may only be filed with the ARIPO Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable filing offices and demarcates where divisionals may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted filing methods (AI 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patent applications may be filed in writing, by delivery by hand, by post or by technical means of communication at the ARIPO Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office hours (8:00–16:30) noted; electronic, fax and physical filings handled under separate rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by facsimile rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be filed by facsimile with ARIPO or competent national authorities of Contracting States that permit fax filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transmitted document is illegible/incomplete it is treated as not received to that extent; written confirmation required only where documents are of inferior quality; ARIPO will invite applicant to supply legible documents within a non-extendable one-month period or application will be refused; applicants asked to label paper confirmations to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing (Rule 5 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patent applications may be filed with ARIPO in electronic form either online or on electronic data carriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement of online submissions will be electronic; procedures for failed transmissions require alternate acknowledgement transmission where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal by receiving Office (Section 2(3), 2(5), Rule 13, AI 34(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The industrial property office of a Contracting State is obliged to forward to the ARIPO Office, in the shortest time compatible with national secrecy, applications filed before it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A time limit of one month after filing is specified for onward transmission for subject-matter obviously not liable to secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application numbering systems (Rule 13(iii), AI 32 and AI 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO application numbers consist of letters AP/P, the last two digits of the year and a five-digit sequential number; receiving offices use two-letter country code then AP/P and internal number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent identification and prevents duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to file an application (Section 2(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be filed by any natural or legal person, or any equivalent to a legal person; may be in the name of one person or several joint applicants; applicant deemed to be entitled to exercise the right to the ARIPO patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another person is adjudged entitled, they may prosecute the application in place of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure on filing — receipts and acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed with ARIPO, the Office must mark each document and the lodging schedule with date of receipt without obliterating content; lodging schedule should include applicant's/representative's reference. Online receipts acknowledged electronically during submission session; alternative acknowledgement if transmission failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When application forwarded by national office, ARIPO notifies applicant of ARIPO receipt and all further documents must be sent directly to ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on filing — minimum requirements for date of filing (Rule 14,15, AI 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: To accord a date of filing, documents must contain: (i) an indication that an ARIPO patent is sought; (ii) designation of at least one Contracting State; (iii) information identifying the applicant; and (iv) a description and one or more claims. Documents must be sufficiently legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of prescribed Request Form No. 3 best provides the indication that a patent is sought; contents of description and claims do not require close scrutiny at this stage—only identification that they appear to be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiencies at filing and rectification period (Rule 15, AI 31(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If deficiencies prevent according a date of filing, the Formality Section communicates them and invites remedy within a non-extendable period of one month; failure to remedy causes the application not to be dealt with as an ARIPO application or to be deemed withdrawn depending on context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific time limits for different deficiencies are set elsewhere; Formality Section should raise all formal deficiencies in its first report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing determination (Rule 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of filing is the date the application meets the minimum requirements and is either (i) date of receipt at ARIPO or competent national authority; or (ii) the date within the one-month period on which applicant rectifies deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rectification defines filing date, applicant informed of the date accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of filing and designation fees (Rules 11(2),(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing and designation fees shall be paid in U.S. dollars direct to ARIPO or application accompanied by an undertaking to pay within 21 days; national offices may accept local currency equivalents in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees unpaid within normal period may still be paid within a non-extendable grace period of one month with surcharge; communications about fees should be issued only after filing date is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation into English (Section 2(6), Rule 5(2), AI 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation into English must be filed within the time limit specified (the Guidelines state 'within 2 after the filing of the application' — see implementing regulations for exact period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation missing, applicant invited to supply it; failure may affect processing/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination subject-matter (Rule 15 and AI 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalities Section examines compliance with Harare Protocol formal requirements relating to: (i) representation; (ii) physical requirements of the application; (iii) abstract; (iv) request for grant; (v) claim to priority; (vi) designation fees; (vii) designation of inventor; and (viii) filing of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities staff should refer to other Parts (esp. Part V) as necessary; formalities officers must ensure uniform and expeditious handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirements (Section 2(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation is required where an application is filed directly with ARIPO but applicant's ordinary residence or principal place of business is not in the host country, or if filed with national office by an applicant whose ordinary residence is not in a Contracting State; authorization (if required) must be in order and filed in due time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance effects and actions are governed by Rule 15(2); formalities staff must ensure representation formalities are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements of documents (Section 3(2)(a), AI 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents making up the application (request, description, claims, abstract, drawings) must meet the form requirements of AI 26(1–9) to enable reasonably uniform publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formality Section responsible for ensuring requirements met; replacement documents and translations follow same form rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of subsequent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document submitted by the applicant after transmittal to ARIPO shall be filed directly with ARIPO; Instruction 26(1) applies to documents forming part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids delays and misrouting—applicants must send post-filing papers to ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements (Rule 5(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed after filing the application (except annexed documents) must be signed by applicant or representative; the Request for Grant must be signed by the applicant or his representative (each applicant if multiple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to sign may constitute a deficiency requiring rectification within set period; naming of inventor documents must be signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant form requirements (Rule 5(5), AI 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for grant must be made on ARIPO Form No.3 and must contain the information listed in Rule 5(5) (name, address, nationality etc.). Applicants allowed to correct deficiencies in the request; use latest version of form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form is integral; ARIPO may publish new versions and recommends always using latest form available on website/Official Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming (designation) of inventor (Rule 5(5)(e), AI 15) and related rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor shall be named unless he files a written declaration that he wishes not to be named; designation must contain surname, given names, full address, statement of origin of right and signature of applicant/representative; ARIPO does not verify accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major deficiencies (missing inventor name or signature) lead to communication and potential deemed withdrawal if not remedied within minimum two months; minor deficiencies invite correction; incorrect designation can be rectified with consents; cancellation/rectification procedures set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority — entitlement and requirements (Section 2(7),(8), Rules 8, AI 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant entitled to claim priority where: (i) previous application filed in recognized State; (ii) applicant is same or successor in title; (iii) ARIPO application filed within 12 months from first filing; (iv) ARIPO application is for same invention as previous application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous application can be patent/utility model/inventor's certificate; priority can be claimed from national, regional or international applications; transfer of priority must have occurred before later filing; multiple priorities allowed with time limits measured from earliest priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and proof of priority (Rule 8, AI 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant claiming priority must file declaration indicating date, State and file number of previous application; copy of previous application (priority document) must be filed before end of 16 months from date of priority, certified as exact copy and accompanied by certificate stating filing date; some exceptions (e.g., previous ARIPO application or PCT filed with ARIPO) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file declaration or priority document in time constitutes deficiency and may lead to loss of priority; file number must be indicated before end of the sixteenth month after priority date or be treated as deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss/non-entitlement to right to priority and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: No priority right arises if application not filed within 12 months and applicant hasn't corrected date or re-established rights, or if previous application did not give rise to a priority right; right to priority is lost where declaration or copy/translation not filed in due time. Applicant is notified of non-entitlement or loss and time limits are recomputed accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of priority does not affect time limits already expired; procedures for notification and possible re-establishment apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention requirements (Rule 6(1)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title must clearly and concisely state the technical designation of the invention and exclude fancy names, personal names, the word 'patent', trade names/trademarks, vague titles such as 'Method' alone, and the abbreviation 'etc.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formality Section should avoid publication of clearly non-informative or misleading titles; Examining Division has ultimate responsibility and ARIPO may change the title if necessary, notifying applicant before publication if title changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement (Section 3(1)(a)(ii), Rule 5(1)(e), AI 24 and 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every application must contain an abstract; if none provided, ARIPO will invite applicant to supply one or pay prescribed fee for ARIPO to prepare the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract is necessary for publication and searching; ARIPO can prepare at applicant's cost if applicant fails to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States and designation fees (Section 3(1)(a)(iii), Rule 5(1)(f), AI 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: All designated States must be Contracting States to the Harare Protocol at the filing date; designation fees must be paid on filing or within 21 days; insufficient designation fees require applicant to indicate for which states fees apply or ARIPO will apply to first-designated states; failure to pay leads to deemed withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation may be withdrawn up to grant; fees not refunded when designation withdrawn; designation cannot be withdrawn if third party has initiated entitlement proceedings and up to ARIPO resuming proceedings for grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO-PCT entry-phase designation fees and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: For ARIPO-PCT applications entering the ARIPO phase, designation fees must be paid upon entry or within 21 days. If no designation fee paid within basic period the ARIPO patent application is deemed withdrawn; omitted acts may be remedied within two months from notification (or extension requested subject to fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO applies PCT provisions in addition to Harare Protocol; time limits and re-establishment rules differ where PCT prevails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of formal deficiencies (Section 3(2)(b), Rule 15(2), AI 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examination finds deficiencies that may be corrected, the Formality Section must give the applicant opportunity to rectify each deficiency within a specified period; the Formality Section should in the first report raise all formal deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deficiencies not rectified in due time the application may be refused or deemed withdrawn; minor deficiencies may be corrected with invitation to correct; further processing or re-establishment may be possible on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and notifications (Part V: 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should be sent to inform applicant/representative of deficiencies, invite observations or documents, inform that patent cannot be granted/maintained without amendment, communicate information necessary for proceedings, or notify when decision is based on grounds parties had no opportunity to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each communication may prolong prosecution—effort should be made to issue as few communications as possible and to cover all necessary points in a single communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to application content (6.1.1 / Part V)
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of an ARIPO application, patent or registered utility model may be amended within limits laid down in the Harare Protocol. Amendments are normally made by submitting missing documents or replacement pages; replacement pages should clearly identify all amendments and indicate passages of the original they are based on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear identification of changes promotes procedural efficiency and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits, extensions and loss of rights (Rule 15bis; Part V 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harare Protocol imposes specified time limits; ARIPO may set periods where not specified. Time limits are usually specified in full months and may be extended if applicant requests extension in writing before expiry; long extensions (>6 months total) allowed only exceptionally with convincing reasons. Failure to act can lead to loss of rights; affected persons may request a decision by ARIPO within 2 months of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute time limits from receipt of communications; re-establishment and further processing may be possible under conditions set by Protocol/Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT application handling (Part V 5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO may act as a designated or elected office for PCT international applications; PCT provisions apply in addition to Harare Protocol and prevail in case of conflict (e.g., certain time limits). ARIPO may also act as a receiving office; initial processing and formal examination are carried out in accordance with PCT receiving office guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ARIPO is receiving office, employees follow PCT receiving office guidelines; national law may require filing via national authority as intermediary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnology/chemistry disclosure sufficiency — definition of proteins and polypeptides
rubrics_metrics.description: Proteins may be claimed by explicit amino acid sequence (SEQ ID NO) or by referring to derived proteins (substitution/deletion/addition) combined with functional definition, but derived proteins are permissible only if: I. the derived protein is exemplified in the description (e.g., examples); and II. the description states technical means for producing and verifying its function; otherwise disclosure is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sequence-based or function-based claim formats are used, the description must enable production and verification; alternative descriptors (function, physicochemical properties, origin, source, production process) may be used when sequence/function formats cannot be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotech claim drafting — monoclonal antibodies and hybridomas
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim directed to a monoclonal antibody may be defined by specifying the hybridoma which produces it (for example, 'a monoclonal antibody produced by a hybridoma having deposit no. xxx').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit information (access number, depositary) is acceptable to identify biological material; defining antibodies solely by function/epitope requires support to establish novelty and inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism claim description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A microorganism claim shall be described according to microbiological taxonomic denomination with Latin name in brackets when first mentioned; if deposited, the deposit institution abbreviation and access number should be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a specific mutant strain is not described in the application, a claim for that mutant strain is not permissible; claims for 'derivative' are potentially indefinite and unclear about scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and inventive step standards in genetic engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty and inventive step for genes, recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, vectors, transformants, fused cells and microorganisms are assessed case-by-case: e.g., a gene is novel if its protein is novel; a recombinant protein identical in amino acid sequence to a known purified protein lacks novelty; inventive step generally lacking when claimed combinations are predictable from known components unless unexpected technical effects are shown; for microorganisms, new taxonomic characteristics or unexpected technical effects support inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must consider whether a person skilled in the art could readily derive the claimed subject-matter from prior art and whether unexpected technical effects are credibly disclosed or demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability in biotechnology
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotechnology inventions that cannot be repeated do not possess practical applicability and shall not be granted patent rights. Processes for screening particular microorganisms from the natural environment are generally not repeatable and therefore not practically applicable unless applicant provides sufficient evidence of repeatability. Processes for producing new microorganisms by random mutagenesis similarly require evidence that desired microorganisms can be definitely produced under certain mutagenic conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide sufficient evidence (examples, reproducible methods) to demonstrate repeatability and practical applicability for biotechnological inventions to be allowable.
